utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I think that we -- the witness could be brought into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I'd like to inquire with you, Mr. Weber, whether your assessment of the time you'd need is still the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is not, Your Honour. The Prosecution would estimate approximately 45 minutes for redirect. This is based largely on matters which arose after the Chamber last inquired as to my estimate yesterday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under those circumstances, Mr. Bakrac, the first session plus 15 minutes; 45 minutes for Mr. Weber; and then we have, although limited, time for questions by the Judges or further questions by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that, doesn't come as a surprise, that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Bakrac will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, yesterday we stopped when we were discussing a document. You said that often times it's difficult to distinguish between the Serbian Volunteer Guard and the Serbian Guard. I looked into that --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I correct you, please. That's not what I said. I said that the term "Serbian Guard" has been used -- I mean, I remember at least one document where Serbian Guard was used for Serbian Volunteer Guard, but otherwise I have not seen, at least on the basis of the documents I have reviewed, confusion between these two very distinct groups. However, I have also seen in the various documents I consulted in order to prepare this report that the term "Srpska Garda" or "Serbian Guard" at least on the basis of my experience is not always used for the group that was affiliated with the SPO, the Serbian Renewal Movement of Vuk Draskovic, i.e., that the term is also used for other groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Theunens. So we can assume that the list we looked at yesterday was probably related to the Serbian Guard which belonged to the SPO, but you do allow for the possibility that it is a different organisation which called itself the Serbian Guard; is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- first, personally I would leave out the word "probably." It can be the SPO-affiliated Serbian Guard; it can also be another one. I would have to look into the document and try to find related documents for that time-period, that region, in order to establish the affiliation of that Serbian Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Fine, Mr. Theunens. We'll move on. I only consider it important to look at financing sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at a Prosecution document, which is an exhibit, P1338.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is the 5th Corps command. General Vladimir Vukovic signed the document. It's a strictly confidential document, encrypted, dated the 8th of March, 1992. It deals with precisely the Serbian Guard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, is it a confidential document?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't see a notification to that effect. I may be mistaken. It -- the contents say that it's a confidential document, but I don't think it's a confidential document in terms of it being shown in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is okay to be public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the commander of the 2nd Military District is sent a strictly confidential memo. Under item 1, Branislav Lainovic is referred to, a civilian from Novi Sad, a resident at Nardnog Fronta number 20. Do you know who Branislav Lainovic was in the relevant time-period? Or Branislav Lainovic, also known as Dugi.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no precise recollection, Your Honours. I believe that he played a role in the recruitment of volunteers, but I cannot recall exactly if that is the same Lainovic for which party or which organisation he carried out his activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I put it to you that he did that for the Serbian Renewal Movement and the Serbian Guard we referred to earlier on. We can find the relevant paragraph. It's the last paragraph on page 1 in B/C/S. In English, it's at the top of page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It's at the very top: "In the second half of last year and in January of this year, at the request of the SSNO first, second, third and political administrations, I admitted Serb Guard groups that arrived at the battle front on a number of occasions, assigning them to corps units, where they carried out combat tasks under unified insignia and unity of command. I deemed this kind of assistance only natural, as there have been similar cases to this day." Can we conclude on the basis of this document that the volunteers of the Serbian Guard, that's to say the volunteers of the Serbian Renewal Movement, with the help of the organisation of the SSNO and the army, went to the front line as volunteers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we discussed this document also with Mr. Jordash - and it's also mentioned in my report on page 24 of part 3 - you have to link what is at the top of page 2 with the bottom of page 1 and then look at the context of the SFRY Presidency Order 73. And when we look at that context, this document is consistent with the order, i.e., volunteers who have been initially gathered or recorded by the Serbian Guard, they are integrated in JNA units, and as it is stated at the end of the first paragraph on page 2, "under unified insignia and integral," in military terminology that would be single, under single, i.e., JNA command. And that's exactly what Order 73 from the 10th of December, 1991, states.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, I was just about to ask you what the date of the presidential order was. So that's the 10th of December, 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And it's P1088. And you can find it on pages 116 and following, in part 1 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your question was whether on the basis of this document we could establish that the unit you mentioned went to the frontline. Now, we got an answer which is about a totally different thing, whether this is consistent with other documents. The one is a factual question, the other one is -- the answer is about the consistency and the explanation of what is explained in this document. Now, unless you are not interested in the factual question itself, then we can move on, but I just observe that what you asked is not what your answer was about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document -- Your Honours, I apologise for the extensive answer, but I wanted to specify the question. And, okay, as the first paragraph states, that in this particular situation, according to the document, indeed, these volunteers were under the conditions set out in that paragraph sent to the front line where they carried out combat tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Theunens, you will agree that the document states, in the second half of last year, i.e., 1991 and in January 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the first paragraph of page 2, says that in the second half year they were sent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was my answer also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- thought that you deviated in any way from what is said here. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we call up 2D297.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this was one of the documents I gave you on the CD; do you recognise it? It's the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, state security department. The date is 9 March 1993, and it's a report on the activities of the Serbian Guard in Eastern Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The document has two pages and I'll try to summarise its contents. The state security department establishes that the Serbian Guard Volunteers, under the command of Osmajlic at the time in Eastern Herzegovina close to Boracko lake, that there they managed to link up with the Defence structure in Eastern Herzegovina and with the command of the eastern corps and that a staff was set up under the functional command of Boro --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: -- who had been promoted recently to the rank of major of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last name which the interpreters could not catch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I said that this particular staff of the Serbian Guard, specifically Zvonko Osmajlic as its commander, were under the functional command of Boro Antelj, who had just been promoted to the rank of major within the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Have you come across information of this sort, i.e., that in this particular period the Serbian Guard was active in this area of Herzegovina under the command of Boro Antelj?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you don't remember, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 2D257, please. While we're waiting for it to appear on our screens, I will identify the document, to use up the time that I have. So it's the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Serbian province of Semberija and Majevica, Brcko municipality. 18th June, 1991, is the date. This is a request for the purposes of the Brcko special unit. So it's a request which was signed by Captain Sasa Vukojevic, the commander of the special unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, as we can see here, from their own municipality, Brcko municipality, within the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, they request camouflage uniforms of the American make, American belts, and -- and dark red berets. I'm showing you this because it is the Prosecution case that individuals wearing American uniforms were most likely connected to the DB of Serbia which procured those for their purposes. Can you tell me, while you were present in the territory of Slavonia, did you have occasion to see such American uniforms? Can you tell us what they were like? And did you have information to the effect that in Bosnia-Herzegovina their special units were being equipped or provided with American uniforms and dark red berets?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours -- I mean, [indiscernible] answer the question, but the document we have in front of us does not seem to be the document you are talking about, because this document is dated 21st of June, 1992, and at least on this page there's no reference to --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was looking at my hard copy without paying attention to the screen. 2D257. Page 2. Yes, in fact it's page 2 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We'll go back to page 1 later on and we'll see that it has to do with the Army of Republika Srpska. Or perhaps I should simplify my question, Mr. Theunens. While you were drafting your report, did you come across information or evidence indicating that there existed a special unit in Brcko which wore red berets and American uniforms and was under the command of Sasa Vukojevic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at the Brcko section of my report now. I cannot answer your question as to whether or not there was a VRS special unit in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 1 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that such a unit did exist but you simply overlooked it, and I don't mean it in any disrespectful way, that you simply didn't have enough information about the existence of such a unit while you were making your report? So we can see the heading states the Army of Republika Srpska, Brcko special unit.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: P1083, as it quoted on page 95 of part 3 of the report, discusses a unit of red berets located in the Brcko district and its commanded by, I quote, "so-called Ziko Crnogorac." And then the text continues, stating that: "... further operative work showed that those units were the units under the command of the state security police of Serbia and that their members were mostly from Serbia." That is the information I have found on the presence of a unit that could be described as a special unit in the district -- in the Brcko district, in 1992. But I --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, that's precisely what my question is about. I am confronting you with a piece of evidence referring to the Red Berets, to a Brcko special unit, Sasa Vukojevic signed the document and he seeks to obtain American uniforms from his municipality. So my question is: On the basis of which information did you arrive at the conclusion which is in your report that Ziko Ivanovic Crnogorac was active in Brcko as were members of the MUP or DB of the Republic of Serbia? What was the evidence underlying that conclusion? And I'm asking you this now that I've confronted you with this document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's also P1085, which is footnote 288 in part 3 of the report, which is a certificate signed by Zivojin Ivanovic or Ziko Crnogorac, I mean the nickname, where he signs as the SAO Semberija and Majevica unit for special purposes Brcko commander. So ideally I would have the opportunity to conduct searches on Captain Sasa Vukojevic in order to establish which unit he is commanding and whether or not it's the same unit as the unit of Zivojin Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Theunens, the unit of Zivojin Ivanovic and the evidence you mention states "SAO Semberija and Majevica," the unit for special purposes Brcko. Where in this document do you find that this unit of Zivojin Ivanovic's was a unit under the command of, affiliated to, or whatever you like to term it, with the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to get organised again. There are apparently two issues. One is the evidence on which Mr. Theunens concludes that the special-purposes unit he mentioned, whether that's linked to the MUP of Serbia; that's one question. And another question is whether the unit you are referring to in this document is the same unit or a different unit. Let's try to clearly separate those two questions. If it is the same unit, the answers in relation to the links to the MUP of Serbia may be relevant. If it is a different unit, then the answers for the one unit would not apply for the other unit, and then, as Mr. Theunens said, you would have to look into the -- any documentation on the special unit which was commanded by Vukojevic. That's -- the only thing at this moment I'm doing is trying to clearly define what the questions are. And, Mr. Bakrac, you introduce another unit and then you switch to -- again to the unit Mr. Theunens dealt with where he says, I would have to find out whether we are talking about two different units or whether it's the same, and you are switching from the one to the other in a bit of an unclear manner. Could you please ask focused questions and clearly separate separate issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Let me formulate the question like this:

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From the document that you are referring to, 1085, from this document signed by Zivojin Ivanovic, can you tell me how, on the basis of this document, one can conclude that he commands a unit which has any relation whatsoever with the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, before I answer the question, I would just like to clarify the document we have in front of us. It doesn't necessarily state that Vukojevic is the commander. He signs for the command. Now, we would first have to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a detail which seems not to be of primary relevance at this moment. It may be an element in deciding whether or not we are talking about the same document, which certainly is a question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Now, P1085 is dated the 9th of July, 1992, and when we compare and we look at P1085 which indeed does not mention MUP Serbia but we apply the methodology and we compare it with P1083, well, in P1083 -- in P1083, Ziko Crnogorac is described or identified as a commander of a unit of Red Berets whereby it is stated that the units are under the command of the state security police of Serbia. And I haven't stated in my report that the the SAO Semberija and Majevica units for special purposes of Brcko is a MUP Serbia unit, but when we combine the two, we have, I believe, the same situation as we had over the previous days, i.e., that units which are initially identified as units of MUP Serbia, we see stamps stating that they are MUP Krajina units, a few months later they are MUP RS units, but the unit itself, the individuals, the commander, do not change. So it -- in my view, it's just a matter of changing names for reasons --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But how do you know this, Mr. Theunens? Please give me at least one reference that would serve as a basis for what you are saying now. How can you claim this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Claim what, Mr. Bakrac, that the composition remained the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or that Mr. Ivanovic -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, my apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That -- that the names only changed and that the composition remained the same, if I understood you properly, and that functionally they remained one in the the same thing but with a different name. How do you know, and on the basis of what can you draw such a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, when we looked yesterday at 2D269, I mean the personnel file of Vasilije Mijovic, and I looked at the different documents included in that file and we compare those with the other documents that discuss involvement of Mijovic and people under his command in operations in Croatia, and later Bosnia-Herzegovina, I come to the conclusion that it's the same unit. When I say "the composition remains the same," I cannot claim that the name of each member remains the same, but as is stated in P1083, that these units are manned or that the members are mostly from Serbia. Because, in fact, I mean, that's the conclusion in my report, in fact these are MUP Serbia special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Theunens, I have to move on. But now just to link up documents, I will now go back to a document which we looked at yesterday, that's P1083.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a look at the second page and the penultimate paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the document to show up on the screen, Mr. Theunens, you explained why in your report and you referred to a 2D document which you only had a chance to see over the weekend and you say that you draw your conclusion from that. So the 2D document referring to Vasilije Mijovic is something you didn't have before the weekend, and you didn't have it at your disposal when you are drafting your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct that 2D269 I only had during the weekend, but 2D269 is a personnel file. Where there are different documents indicating the activities of in this case Vasilije Mijovic over the years. And I could link these documents with the other documents I had seen where -- I mean, other documents are individual orders, situation reports, requests, reports compiled by intelligence organs both from the JNA as well as from the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska. And when you combine all that, I mean, it's -- it becomes -- the picture becomes much clearer. So 2D269 allowed me to obtain a much clearer picture than I already had before but it corroborates -- or and it corroborates the conclusions I had drawn in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, for all clarity, P1083 is a confidential document. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Theunens, please look at the second paragraph. "Operative work in the field," that is how it begins. Mr. Theunens, please focus, as we are now focused on a specific issue. Focus on the second paragraph where it says that the information is not sufficient and needs to be checked, about the unit of Ziko Crnogorac, and it is suggested that the real leader of Red Berets in the territory of Republika Srpska was a man nicknamed Sasa. We have seen a document in which Vukojevic, Sasa requests from his municipality American uniforms. Can you see that in this document, please? And can this help you to establish a connection? It has not been recorded, but we can all read it. However for the the needs of the record, it says there that the report states that the information just needs to be collected and that this is just some circumstantial evidence. So would you agree with me that this person suspects that the actual leader is one Sasa? I have presented you a document which has to do with a commander called Sasa Vukojevic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see the reference in the text to a Sasa, and I have discussed a person nicknamed Sasa in my report, but this information does not affect what is mentioned in relation to Zika Crnogorac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. I have to move on in order to cover at least what I believe I have to cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] could we now please have a look at 2D319.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This was a document that the Prosecution had no notice of prior to yesterday. The Chamber did inquire with Mr. Bakrac as to when he became aware of the use of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: His investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And we -- yes. And we -- well, we did conduct discussions with a language assistant. There -- this is a rather cryptic report dealing -- and I don't want to say too much because of the witness witness's presence, a rather cryptic report that deals with a conversation had by Captain Dragan. The available translation is only a partial translation. There are many references that the Prosecution believes are important, would be important for this witness's testimony, in order to ascertain what is being said that are not reflected in the translation. The witness does not speak B/C/S, and Prosecution believes that, one, it is prejudiced because it was not provided with the complete translation; this affects our ability to re-examine on this document because effectively, due to the nature of the document and its content being a rather cryptic conversation that mentions other important individuals that are not reflected in the partial translation, we essentially have to make representations as to what is being said, which we do not want to do. And also it prevents the expert from reviewing the entire document and providing the expert's opinion in the context of his entire report, since a complete translation is not available. So we also did check, and Mr. Laugel informed us that the document was uploaded and available in e-court on the 29th of October, 2010, which would have been last Friday. We did receive multiple notifications from the Simatovic Defence after that. The document was not included in those notifications. We ask that the Defence be not allowed to use this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, when did you investigator get hold of this document, and where does it come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I used the break to work, and I ordered my investigator to carry out certain investigative measures, and I returned on the 25th to The Hague. And after that I cannot remember, but I think that it was on the 27th or the 28th that I received this document. I uploaded it immediately. And when I saw that we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why not just answer my question? You come with a speech of half an hour. I asked when your investigator got hold of this document. That was my question. Not on whether you sent him for -- that's a simple question. If you know, tell us; if you don't know, tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said that he came into the possession of this document after the weekend, that is to say, in the week beginning on the 25th of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't say that. You said you received it after the weekend, after you had given him instructions to investigate. Now, whether those instructions to investigate resulted in this document to be obtained, you didn't say anything about that. But let's leave that alone. So could you tell us where the document comes from?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the source of this document is a potential witness from AOS, which is American Intelligence Service; it's an abbreviation for one section of it, as you will see here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you received it from a -- what you called a potential witness. May I take it, then, a potential Defence witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If you allow me, Your Honour, because my time is running out, I can just read it. Let me not deal with the contents, because later on we can all read what is in there, but please allow me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, have you not heard what is the major concern of Mr. Weber? That he has only a partial translation, that the witness is not in a position to review the whole of the document, and that therefore we are more or less limping, we are handicapped. That's -- I suggest that you -- let me just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the Chamber does not allow you at this moment to put a partial translation of a report which is available to the Prosecution only since -- I'm talking now as relevant in days. But of course, you now have knowledge of the content of parts of this document and you can, without using this document, of course, you can put questions to the witness which -- for which the answers may be relevant at a later stage when you have a full translation and when you have given proper notice to the Prosecution. So the document is not banned forever, but not to be used at this moment under those circumstances. Please proceed. If you want to put questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, please allow me just one comment, and I hope that Mr. Weber will agree, because I did discuss about this with Mr. Weber. I told him that we have some documents which have not been translated, and Mr. Weber told me that it would be useful for them to receive the B/C/S versions because they have personnel in the OTP who speak the B/C/S, just for the record, but I will move on. So, Mr. Theunens -- I suppose I'm addressing Mr. Weber now, so as to be faster: Does this also relate to the document 2D292, the same objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the notice was a little bit different with this, but if there's a partial translation and there's a question being posed to the witness that may encompass greater knowledge or a greater importance than just what is said in the document, we do object. We believe it's unfair to give a partial translation to this witness and ask him to make more general comments without reviewing the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course it all depends on what kind of questions you put to a witness. If you have a partial translation, if you want someone to look at stamps, for example, then a partial translation, in itself, doesn't harm. But it much depends. But if you want to go to the content of the document, if we have -- if there's -- parts are missing, then that's not the way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That was the Prosecution's position.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would -- I don't know if Your Honours are aware, but we receive partial translations of many documents on an on-going basis from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If it is well in advance and if you have an opportunity to check. I mean, we have to find a fair balance between not overburdening our CLSS and so that if it's a matter of efficiency it's fine; but if you come with a document half a day before, if the witness has no opportunity to look at the whole of the document; especially for this witness that's important. I'm not saying that under all circumstances partial translations are not admissible. I'm just saying that under the present circumstances, in relation to these documents, notice given only half a day before a witness who is used to go through the documents in its entirety, if -- that's -- these are circumstances. And, again, this document is not banned, but not to be used at this moment with this witness where questions which are related to the content of whatever documents you have a partial translation of, of course, can be put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted the full picture to be known to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now we have the full picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As my time is running out, Mr. Theunens, let us have a look at 2D295. And while we are waiting for it to show up on the screen, I will suggest to you that I wanted to present to you two documents from the state security administration. One is a document dated the 15th of April, 1991, and the other one dated the 15th of August, 1991, in which the second department of the state security service, the abbreviation for which is AOS, which is American Operative Service, with which Franko Simatovic was involved, was tasked to follow Daniel Snedden, to follow his contacts, and follow the activities of this person through intelligence work. Now, please have a look at this document dated the 15th of August, 1991. Would you agree with me that the minister of the the interior, Zoran Sokolovic made this decision to secretly wire-tap the telephone in a privately-owned apartment used by Daniel Snedden, who is an Australian citizen? And as far as you know and based on your investigations, does this have to do with Captain Dragan, also known as Dragan Vasiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we just scroll the English translation to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about Mr. Snedden to be identical with Captain Dragan?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document states what you -- what you just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Please let us move on to the next document, and that will be 2D317. So we have seen that in the month of August the minister -- and there was an earlier decision suggesting that since April the American Intelligence Service was monitoring Daniel Snedden. Now we have a document dated the 8th of November, 1991. It's 2D317.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The earlier document, is that the document which we just decided that we would not use that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. This is a document which I think there is no reason not to use. But I wanted to show two previous similar documents which we will use earlier, because Mr. Weber objected. And this one, 2D295, is a document which I believe OTP does not object to at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if counsel could just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's -- Mr. Bakrac, you said: "So we have seen that in the month of August the minister -- and there was an earlier decision" - and I think you said document - "suggesting that since April the American Intelligence Service was monitoring Daniel Snedden." Which document you had on your mind when you referred to this early decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the document from April is a document that we agreed I could not use, so I just wanted to mention that there was an earlier minister's decision by which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I want to know, if you are talking about the earlier decision, which document are you talking about? The document which shows that the American Intelligence Service was monitoring Daniel Snedden, what's the number of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honours, just to clarify, maybe I was not clear because I wished to speed up. This was the Serbian state security service and a group which was called American Intelligence Service or the American Group. It was the one that monitored Snedden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have a document ID or exhibit number or anything? I understood your observation to refer to the document we just had on our screen earlier with the -- the -- you said you received through your investigators from a potential witness. Was that the document you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, please allow me to read this. 2D317 is a document that the Prosecutor objected to. It has to do with wire-tapping Daniel Snedden. And the first sentence says: "Pursuant to a decision of the minister of the interior of the Republic of Serbia number 01-233/1/91 of the 3rd of April, 1991." This has been translated, Your Honour. There is a minister's decision dated the 3rd of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you referring to the document of which we only had a partial translation and which we said you couldn't use? Are you referring to that document, Mr. Bakrac? A yes or a no, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm not referring to that document now because my learned friend objected. I'm referring to document 2D295.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could we have that on the screen so that I know what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour requested the document ID, the April decision - that was the one that we objected to - it's 2D319.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And 2D239 -- 237 is ... have we seen that already?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the document was not on the screen, but from 2D319 one can see that on the 3rd of April, 1991, was issued the first order of the minister of the interior to wire-tap Daniel Snedden. These orders or decisions are renewed, and now I will present to you a decision from the month of April by which the same measure is applied, that is to say, wire-tapping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, don't refer to documents which we haven't seen; that's one. Give us an opportunity to look at documents. Second, don't refer to the content of documents of which we decided that they should not be used at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. 2D295.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can we conclude, based on this document, that the minister of the interior issued an order to the effect that Daniel Snedden, i.e., Captain Dragan, should be monitored and wire-tapped?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, to be precise, it talks about monitoring a telephone number and a flat that is used by Snedden. That's what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Mr. Theunens, let's move on. Please have a look at 2D317 now. And please read through it. 2D317. I'll try to summarise it. I don't think you have the document in your report and therefore there's no need for you to look into your report. You can look at it on your screen. Have you had a look, sir?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And I would like to see the bottom of the page or the next page, if there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please. In the Serbian language as well, or in the B/C/S, we want to see the signature and stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is a document filed with the Ministry of Defence on the 8 of November, 1991. Is it fair to say that the document indicates that Captain Dragan was, by minister Lieutenant-General Tomislav Simovic, hired to prepare volunteers and to seek from the Serbian TO command to resolve his status?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please see the first page again, just to make sure that there's no misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sure. Please have a look. I want to direct your attention to the prior approval, prior -- general consent from the chief of the general staff of the SFRY armed forces and the president of the Republic of Serbia. Do you see any mention of the MUP of Serbia in reference to Captain Dragan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can answer that question: It's no. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And to answer your previous question, I see this -- this document more as a proposal or a suggestion by the minister --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's try to keep matters short. Apparently Mr. Bakrac wants to show this document to seek your approval that it's the Ministry of Defence which seeks the assistance of Captain Dragan in recruitment of volunteers and that the MUP is not mentioned in this document. And, of course, the underlying suggestion, which is a totally different one, is that, therefore, Captain Dragan had nothing to do with the MUP, but that's a different matter. This document doesn't say so. We read in this document as I said. Is that, Mr. Bakrac, what you wanted to establish, at least what you wanted to elicit as evidence from the witness? Then we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Now that Mr. Theunens has seen the document, does it change his position with regard to the relationship between Captain Dragan and Frenki Simatovic. Because of an error on my part, I can't put a question to him in relation to the other two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But does it change your position that Frenki Simatovic and Captain Dragan were in the Krajina to pursue the same tasks, or do you stand by your position?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I stand on my position, and I also refer to P1069 and P1066, which provide additional information on relations between Dragan and the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore Mr. Theunens, I put it to you that your report is inaccurate in this part too. Captain Dragan was hired by the army, and the MUP of Serbia, that's to say, the state security, had been monitoring his activities from April when he returned from abroad. Will you agree with my statement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with the second part of your statement, that he has been monitored. And that is also corroborated by P1062 which is discussed in my report on page 95/96 of part 1 of the report, so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's look at D107. It's an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my question was not interpreted correctly, or perhaps I puzzled the interpreters. At any rate, my question was that Captain Dragan was hired by the JNA and the TO and that the MUP of Serbia, state security department, had for a period of time been monitoring his activities as part of their intelligence work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Will you agree with my suggestion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact that, from the answer, that that's the way in which he understood the question, the way in which the interpreters spoke. Therefore, hired by the army, monitored by the MUP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed. I mean, I agree with Your Honours, my answer does not change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have D107 now. I don't think we have it on our screens yet. Or perhaps my assistant has mislabelled the document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D107 is on the screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D is what I'm looking for.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... 2D107.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I wasn't ... it's D107. It's an admitted document. It's an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we have at this moment on the screen is 2D00107, which apparently is not the document Mr. Bakrac is asking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Look at the document, Mr. Theunens. It's a document from the OTP database. I'm interested in the section of your report concerning the Knin Krajina in the second half of 19 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter isn't sure of the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you know, when you were doing your report, that Mr. Milan Babic was, on the 9th of October, 1991 - and this is something that's important for our indictment - issuing an order whereby all the police units in the territory of the Serbian Autonomous Region of the Krajina were re-subordinated to the Territorial Defence command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I have seen this document before, and it is part of what I considered the power struggle between Mr. Milan Babic and Mr. Milan Martic whereby Milan Babic issued a lot of orders which, when put into context, create an impression that he is attempting to impose his authority; whereas, in reality, it -- Milan Martic has more, what I would call de facto authority, whereas Babic tries to confirm his de jure authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, rather than having a political discussion now, I will have a very simple question for you, since I've run out of time: Tell me, do you know, do you have reasons to doubt that this Babic's order had not been implemented?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is, for example, the -- there is the -- the -- I wanted to refer to the situation in Kijevo, but that's in August 1991 where actually the milicija or the MUP of the SAO Krajina is directly subordinated to the JNA and no mention is made of the TO. I haven't seen any documents indicating that we only had units of the SAO Krajina TO and units of the milicija conducting combat operations during fall 1991. The documents I discuss in my report all concerned combat operations under JNA command whereby elements of -- I mean, depending on the area, elements of the TO, of the SAO Krajina, and/or the police --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether the -- you have reasons to believe that the order was not implemented. Let's first establish whether you have such reasons, yes or no; and then we can further ask for those reasons. I think in your answer you said something about a struggle for --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- for power, and that -- that apparently - that's at least how I understood your answer - that might have been a reason not to automatically believe that the order was implemented, because you referred to a series of orders in that context. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That is well understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please focus the further questions, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, did TO and police units - I just wanted to cut this short; I don't have time - in the ensuing fighting in the second half of 1991 in the area of the Knin Krajina act under the command of the Army of the -- or, rather, the Yugoslav People's Army at the time as per orders on the attacks on Sibenik, Zadar, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I explained in my report. I mean, we have to look at the specific documents for the specific combat operations. I mean, when I mean "documents," the orders and the reports about the execution, and there we see how the units operated. And I have included a number of document indicating indeed that MUP of the SAO Krajina and TO of the SAO Krajina, when they participated in combat operations with the JNA, operated under JNA command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I count on the 15 minutes that I suppose I still have, and I need to look at my notes and then stream-line the questions I still have for Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You have your 15 minutes after the break. We'll take a break, and we resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, my learned friend Mr. Weber asked you in his direct examination on the 25th to give your comments on some reports, specifically P1121 and P1122. Because my time is running out, I will not be calling them up. But do you remember P1122 being a report between the 5th and the 6th of August of 1991, the Serbian Autonomous Province of Krajina, the TO Krajina staff, and an order is given to the secretary of the SUP of SAO Krajina, the organ of security, the TO commander, and, finally, it says Frenki; these are the addressees. Is there any need for us to call it up, or do you recall -- do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the document, and an excerpt can be found on page 36 of part 1 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. We can see here that reports are sent to various institutions and that the last addressee is indicated as Frenki, without any supplementary information. And I think that this is within operative intelligence duties that this report is sent to Frenki Simatovic. And I think the same relates or applies to P1121, dated the 15th of July, 1991. Will you agree with me on that score? I suggest that if Franko Simatovic had been institutionalised as part of an organ or an institution, in that case the text would not have simply read "Frenki." Can you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not entirely sure I understand your question, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I -- could I try to rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If a document is address to the "Frenki," which is apparently uncommon for an institutional address, would you agree with that and with the suggestion that if it would have been addressed to an institution, it would not have been addressed to "Frenki"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would have been more usual to put the full name of Frenki as well as the name of the institution. Because there are other circumstances, for example - and I will try to be short - but in 1994, during the latter half of 1994, the RSK sends reports on the situation in the AP WB - and I mean, by that, by RSK; I think it's the Main Staff of the SVK - to a number of addressees, including the minister of interior of the Republic of Serbia, and between bracket then the name of Jovica Stanisic is indicated. The same applies to intelligence reports of the VRS intelligence and security administration in the course of 1994, and that can be found in part 3 of the report. So what I'm saying is you would expect the name of the institution. And if you want to address it to a particular individual in the institution, you use his real name and not a nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Let's look at P1123 now, please. The date -- and this is another report from the Serbian Autonomous Province of Krajina, the Main Staff of the Krajina TO, and the date is 17 September 1991. We can all see that this report is not addressed to Frenki. Did you ever come across a document, outside of the ones you mentioned, which were dated after August 1991 and were sent to Frenki from the SAO Krajina, in addition to the ones we saw from the months of July and August 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would first like to answer your first suggestion, when you say the report is not addressed to Frenki. It is correct that the addressee list does not mention the name "Frenki," but it mentions ODB, so the state security office, without indicating which one. I haven't drawn any conclusions on that because I know there was an SAO Krajina -- or attempts, there were attempts, of an SAO Krajina DB, but I'm not sure to what extent that was operational. So -- and, secondly, I have not seen any other documents for the time-period you indicate that mention the name Frenki in the addressee list.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. A follow-up question on this document: The Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina, the Main Staff of the Krajina TO, and it is sent to the supreme commander of the armed forces of the SAO Krajina, the commander of the armed forces of SAO Krajina, and the chief of the SAO Krajina TO, and the state security organ; you will agree with me that it is only logical for this state security organ to refer to the state security organ of the Krajina if we look at all the other addressees in the document? I can refresh your memory or suggest that P1122, P1121 also have listed as an addressee "ODB," that's to say, state security organ; and my suggestion is that this must relate to the Krajina state security organ rather than state security of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I'm not able to -- as I explained in my previous answer, I'm not able to draw a definite conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Please look at 2D294. We'll wait for it to appear. In direct examination you said - and you'll correct me if I'm wrong --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]So 2D294, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that in this period - and I'm waiting for your translation - it's the 14th of July, 1991 - that there were no commanders or there was no TO commander. Have a look and you'll see that it's Major Dragisic Milan who signed in the capacity of the TO commander. Are you familiar with this? That same TO commander issued an order to the Golubic storage facility that for the purposes of the Glina TO, a certain amount of weapons were to be set aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. Counsel is testifying. If he could just direct his questions towards the material in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you rephrase your question, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you agree with my suggestion that on the 14th of July -- or, rather, in the month of July of 1991 in the area of the SAO Krajina there was a Territorial Defence under the command of commander Dragisic who issued an order that the Golubic storage facility should set aside a certain amount of weapons for the purposes of the Glina TO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we just scroll down to the bottom of the English. Yeah, I can see that, but I have not seen the document before, and my reply during examination was based on the decision, including P959, whereby Milan Babic appoints a commander for the SAO Krajina TO. And, again, based on the other documents I have reviewed, my conclusion is that only in September -- excuse me, only end of September a commander for the SAO Krajina TO staff is appointed. I would have to look in -- I mean, since I haven't seen this document before, I would have to look in the actual competencies of this Major Milan Dragisic. Again, at first glance, it would be unusual to have a major as the commander of the TO of an area as large as the SAO Krajina, knowing that the person who is appointed end of September - and the decision dates from 5th of October - is a retired general of the JNA. Excuse me, is it lieutenant-colonel? Okay, indeed. And he was replaced by a colonel later. But it would be unusual to have a major in that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But Mr. Theunens, you are now talking about the rank, but wasn't Milan Martic at one point appointed as the commander of the Territorial Defence of SAO Krajina -- or, rather, the minister of defence of SAO Krajina? Did he hold the rank and did he have the proper qualifications for such a position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, it seems to me that the focus of your question was not about ranks but about an order being given to set aside, et cetera, et cetera. Now, Mr. Theunens, not surprisingly, focuses on the ranks; that's part of his expertise. And instead of taking him back to what you really wanted to know, you follow him in a discussion on ranks. That's at least how I analyse your questioning. If that's what you want, please go ahead. If, however, it is your intention to get to the core of this document apart from ranks, please do so as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, have you heard of the Alfa Training Centre in Bruska, and was it something that you looked into?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, I have heard of the Alfa Training Centre in Bruska. And there must be documents in part 1 or part 2 of the report discussing the training centre. I'm just trying to locate them now. But maybe Mr. Bakrac can help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, as I only have two or three minutes at my disposal, I will first ask you if there is anything we do not agree about. Would you agree with me that the 107th Training Centre Alfa was a training centre of the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina from its foundation in 1993 all the way to 1995?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a recollection that the training centre already existed prior to the establishment of the SVK, but I'm trying to locate a document to substantiate this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I do not remember that this is included in your report. If it is, please tell me what is the evidence which shows that the Alfa centre in Bruska had existed even before the forming of the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer the question now, but I have a recollection -- but if -- I mean, if my recollection is correct, it's in my report, because I do believe that I have included at least a document, one document, on the Alfa Training Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I will try to refresh your memory, as my time is running out. Perhaps we might resolve the dilemma. I'm not talking about Golubic; I'm talking about the Alfa centre in Bruska. And I suggest to you that there is not a one single document or piece of evidence in your report which would suggest that the Alfa centre in Bruska had existed before the formation of the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Due to a lack of time, I would offer the following documents which testify to the fact that between 1993 and 1995 the Alfa centre in Bruska was a centre of the Army of Republic of Serbian Krajina. These are 2D267, 2D247, 2D248, D71, 2D249, 2D286, and Defence also has other documents but as we do not have enough time, it is sufficient to list these and draw the Trial Chamber's attention to these documents which clearly show whose centre this was and when it was founded.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As my time has run out now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, just to add, there is P1178, which is discussed on page -- on, excuse me, part 2 of page 69 which links Dragan -- or which identifies Captain Dragan as the commander of the Alfa Training Centre, but it's an -- it's an undated report. Based on the context, it would be from after 1994. But, indeed, later, it has -- I mean, at that time-period, it has a military post number. And now when I stand corrected it's -- I mean, document -- yeah, footnote 189 - but there's no P number - states that the training centre was established on the 25th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I take it that -- I suggest to the parties - on this I'm addressing both Mr. Weber and you and perhaps Mr. Jordash as well - that you prepare a kind of a spreadsheet with all the documents, some of them you have now referred to them, we have not seen them, that we do it as if all of the documents were bar table documents. That may be the most practical way of proceeding, that we have any objections in partial translations, whatever, what has been used, that we put that in a kind of a table, comments of the other parties, and then we'll decide on admission. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution was going to suggest that same course today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- well, I should have waited for you then. Mr. Bakrac, you are referring now to a couple of documents; you could include them on your list as well. Because it's clear that you say these documents contradict what the expert said in his report about the Alfa centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. I have shortened my examination. I have more documents, but I respect the time allotted to me, even though there are numerous other documents. If you would allow me to ask just one additional question, but we should move into a private session for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, first of all, before we move into private session. If you have other documents which you wanted to have put to the witness, the structure of your questioning very often was, Have you considered this document; and then that's a document which in your view suggests something which is deviating from what the expert said. And often the expert said, Well, that may be true that this document says this or doesn't say it, but I have set out in my report the reasons why I came to a different conclusion. That's the general structure of the questioning. I suggest to you that if there were other documents you would have wanted to put to the witness, that you could still consider them to include them in the table; to clearly indicate that they have not been put to the witness but that you want, for example, to bar table them; and that, in the explanation of the relevance, you refer to "contradicts conclusion page so and so, Theunens's report." Then we have a context and we can still decide. And of course then the Prosecution can object to it or not, but then we have -- we finally achieve the fullest set of acceptable documentation for the Chamber to rely on. That is my suggestion to you. You want to go into private session for one final question. You know one is one. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Your Honours, I do not know the answer. Perhaps the answer might trigger the need to ask more questions, but I will ask just one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. 45 minutes for you, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, on page 91 to page 109 of yesterday's transcript, you were asked questions related to Vasilije Mijovic. On page 91, lines 24, to page 92, line 4, you indicated that you reviewed 65 ter 2D269 which is now admitted as P1585. You also made reference to this exhibit here today. With respect to this exhibit, when you've discussed it -- and yesterday you stated a number of documents were included that provide information on the different assignments of Mr. Mijovic held between 1991 and 1995 time-period. The Prosecution today would like to start by discussing some of the additional documents which were not presented to you so far during your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If the Prosecution could please have page 20 of the B/C/S original and page 19 of the English translation of Exhibit P1585.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the document that is now appearing before you is a report from the Republic of Serbia MUP, Belgrade Secretariat, dated 15 December 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have page 20 B/C/S; page 19 English.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I apologise. Could this document not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to be made public. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the fourth paragraph in the document that begins "having discussed the matter thoroughly ..." is there any information in this paragraph which describes the employment of Mr. Mijovic with the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. The paragraph states that Mr. Mijovic is employed at the Republic of Serbian MUP, second division, state security service, under Jovica Stanisic. And, okay, I will not read it all out -- out all the details, but then there's a reference to a MUP Serbia identity card which was issued 21st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 32 of the B/C/S and page 30 of the English translation of this Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is an Official Note dated 29 June 1993 from the Republic of Serbia MUP police station for border crossing control in Mali Zvornik. Could you please identify for us the incident that is described on the 29th of June, 1993, the same date of this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, summarised, it's a report by a policeman who was at the border crossing there and who encountered difficulties with Mr. Mijovic, who was driving an Audi 80 vehicle with what appears to be an official licence plate and he was trying to enter FRY from Bosnia-Herzegovina. And I think he refused to be checked or he made problems when he -- when the policeman insisted on checking him or the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You say that there was an official reference to an official licence plate; how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the M 601 896. Now, I'm not able here to say -- I'm not an expert in licence plates, whether it's a MUP Serbia or a MUP RS licence plate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this document, what occurred after Mijovic produced his official ID card?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following a question whether -- as to whether he had weapons, Mijovic replied that he had various weapons and explosive devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What does this Official Note demonstrate?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are various interpretations possible, but it shows, okay, that Mijovic was travelling from Bosnia-Herzegovina to -- to FRY on board of an -- what I saw as an official vehicle, I mean, of a private nature but still officially registered, with weapons and explosives on board, and he refuses to be checked by a regular policeman at the border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 22 of the B/C/S and English of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you -- the last question, what the the Official Note demonstrates, was not focused. And resulted in an answer which brought us nothing new compared to what we had heard already. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in light of the cross-examination questions that were posed to you about the role of the MUP in the border, what does this document demonstrate to you specifically?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It shows that at least at the date of the document the MUP of the Republic of Serbia is controlling the incoming traffic, i.e., traffic moving from Bosnia-Herzegovina, so from the territory held by the Bosnian Serbs towards Serbia here at Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is a candidate questionnaire dated 11 December 1995 signed by Vasilije Mijovic from his JSO personnel file. Directing your attention to the entry for "job position and information on career in the service to date," what does Vasilije Mijovic himself indicate as the answer in this questionnaire?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He states that since 1991 he is in the JATD. And my conclusion is this is the JATD of the MUP of Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this questionnaire at all, does Mr. Mijovic say he was re-assigned or transferred or subordinated to another institution?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe if we can -- I mean, on this, what I see on the screen, not; but if we move downwards, no, there's -- I don't see such a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... it's many pages, this document. I invite the parties to agree on whether it says or doesn't say that he moved to any other -- when reading the document, which I did once, I didn't find any such reference to it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to the last three documents that I showed you today and in the context of the exhibits shown to you by the Defence yesterday and the documents referenced in your report, could you please tell us what your opinion would be on Mr. Mijovic's employment between 1991 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat what I stated yesterday and even also this morning that between 1991 and 1995, in this case we are looking at Vasilije Mijovic, he is an employee of the MUP Serbia, even if there are documents suggesting that the units he's commanding during the time-period belong to local Serb MUP. Some documents are RSK MUP or SAO Krajina MUP, other documents Republika Srpska MUP. But, in fact, he is always a member of the MUP Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: One last document that I would like to discuss with you based on what you just said in your last answer ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 29 of the B/C/S and page 27 of the English of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is a list of personnel who have Krajina MUP ID cards. For the record, could you please read off the first four names on this list.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number one, Zivojin Ivanovic; number 2, Radojica Bozovic; number 3, Nikola Loncar; number 4, Vasilije Mijovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the context of the opinion that you just expressed on page 43, lines 6 through 12 of today's transcript, could you please tell us what this document indicates?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ideally I would have to see the same forms for these three other individuals as we did for Vasilije Mijovic, but in the absence of that, I would still conclude that also these other people, again, based on the documents I have reviewed during the preparation of my report, that also these three other individuals are members of the MUP Serbia throughout the relevant time-period, even if there are other documents that associate them with local MUP - I mean, SAO Krajina, RSK, or RS MUP - during that time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 74, line 10, to page 77, line 7 of yesterday's transcript, you were asked questions about Radojica Raja Bozovic. On page 76, lines 8 to 11, you were asked whether you came across a piece of evidence or a document proving that Raja Bozovic was in the Serbian MUP at all at any time and especially in 1994 and 1995. In the course of this examination, you were shown 65 ter 2D65 which the Defence submitted indicates that Mr. Bozovic was a part of the RS MUP. The Prosecution would like to discuss with you another Defence exhibit that was provided to you on the CD --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I haven't even said what the exhibit is. If we could at least --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I'm going to say that could Mr. Stanisic go to the restroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would -- I take that he we prefer that we continue, or?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We can continue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Then, thank you. Because we would stop if Mr. Stanisic would insist on that or even asked for that, Mr. Jordash. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would like to discuss with you another exhibit that was provided to you in notice to the Prosecution by the Simatovic Defence for your cross-examination but not discussed with you throughout your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 2D268. This is the JSO personnel file of Raja Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, did you have occasion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to be shown to the public?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you for reminding me. If we could please not broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, did you have occasion to review this file and the materials that were provided to you by the Simatovic Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, and I didn't remember the exact contents of this file or this document when answering the question yesterday in relation to 1994/1995 documents on Radojica Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 8 of the B/C/S and page 7 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This document that now appears before you is a recommendation for hiring from the JATD Deputy Commander Milan Radonjic. Could you please tell us what the first paragraph of this document indicates?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a proposal to -- that is submitted. A proposal submitted to hire Radojica Bozovic pursuant to a decision of the minister of interior of the republic. And this decision dates the 4th of August, 1993. And the specific nature of the position he is proposed for is indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this document, does it indicate that he is -- that's with respect to a permanent employee position?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I missed that, I'm sorry. It's a permanent employee position in the ATD of the RDB.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 9 of the B/C/S and page 8 of the English translation of this exhibit. The Prosecution notes that a similar document has already been admitted. I can provide the P number at a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
