utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is a request for operative vetting dated 28 February 1992 from the state security service of Serbia to the MUP of Montenegro. Could you please tell us if there's any pertinent information contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document mentions the name Radojica Bozovic, and according to the document he is -- on the 28th of February, 1992, he is an employee of the revenue administration in the municipality of Tito Grad, Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does this document indicate what unit the vetting is on behalf?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. It's on behalf of the special unit of the -- of the MUP of Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And according to the document, who is indicated as the signatory?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the SDB state security service Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 5 of the B/C/S and page 4 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you please just take a second and look at this document and then identify it for the record.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, the title, Your Honours, the title is clear; it's a background-check report on Radojica Bozovic, and it's dated 27th of October, 1993, state security service, Podgorica sector, i.e., the Republic of Montenegro, minister of interior who prepares it, it seems.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 6 of the B/C/S and page 5 of the English translation. It is the next page of this report. Specifically if we could have the lower half of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does the last paragraph above the section 3 of this document indicate who requested the background check on Raja Bozovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, sector 2 of the SDB, in view of Bozovic's candidacy for employment in the MUP Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "According to sources, he was wounded several times, especially during the fighting in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in which he stayed the longest. According to the information at our disposal, Radojica is currently staying at a camp (Karadordjevo has been mentioned) where he is involved in training and preparing Special Forces. According to an unverified source, this is a paramilitary formation belonging to one of the parties." Mr. Theunens, could you please analyse this information and the information in the two previous documents I showed you today in the context of the exhibits you cite in your report concerning Raja Bozovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's a similar situation as we discussed with Vasilije Mijovic. Obviously the reports have to be seen in context, and, for example, I haven't seen many references that Bozovic is identified as Crnogorac, his usual nickname is Kobac; but overall the information, i.e., on the presence in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina to participate in combat operations, is coherent with documents provided by other sources I have included in my report, as well as the information on his membership of the MUP Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to this exhibit, on page 68 of the B/C/S version of 2D268, appears a document with Defence ERN 2D00-3324. The ERN assigned by the ICTY Evidence Unit is also visible on this document as 0609-0241. The Prosecution observes that this personnel file consists of 71 pages, and this -- only this one document in the personnel file is not present in the uploaded translation. The Prosecution does have this document available and translated, and we ask that we call up 65 ter 5161.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, as you have not been able to --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a document from 1998 which is why it wasn't admitted. I don't know if it's relevant for a document relating to 1998 ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Listen to the questions and see. Mr. Weber, you are now aware of the doubts as to the relevance, due to the year. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, as you have not seen a translation of this document, could you please just take a moment and read through the document and let the Chamber know when you've read it.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read through the document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This document is a Republic of Serbia Ministry of Internal Affairs Department of State Security JSO document dated 18 April 1998. It relates to the proposal to decorate five members of the detachment. On page 72, lines 9 through 10 of yesterday's transcript, it was put to you whether or not individuals in the state security may have had ranks. Does this document indicate who it is signed by?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is signed by a Colonel Radojica Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to Raja Bozovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you misrepresent --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- yesterday. I think the issue was whether at a certain point in time they had ranks, and that point in time was not 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand that, and I'm going to other date references contained in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Bakrac, this meets your concerns, I take it? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to Raja Bozovic, does he mention when the MUP reserve forces were first established in this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, he states that they have been members of the MUP reserve since 1991. And then it follows: "... , that is, since the unit" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, it's just reading. It says: "Since 1991, that is, since the unit was first established." So that's clear. I usually answer the questions which are just a matter of reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, does this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just to be fair, I won't have much time for re-examination. Reference is made to somebody who isn't either Bozovic or Mijovic. They are apparently members of a MUP, but which MUP, particularly, is not specified. These are certain individuals who are said to have been members of the MUP in 1991, but we don't have either Ivanovic, Bozovic, Mijovic, or anyone else here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, on the top of this document, it appears that it originates from the Republic of Serbia Ministry of Internal Affairs. So apparently they are, for whatever reason, playing a role in this matter. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I brought up this date reference at the end of the first paragraph because in context of the reference to the anniversary on the 4th of May, which appears earlier in the text, in the other exhibits that you reviewed in your report, particularly section 9 of P1075, what is your analysis of the existence of the special-purpose units or MUP units of the state -- of the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this moment in time I cannot give a precise date, but there are various documents, especially in sections 2 and 3 of the report, that mention special-purpose units of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia -- sorry, that mention the special-purpose unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia at various time-periods at least from 1992 onwards. But I cannot give you a precise date as to the establishment of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender 2D268 into --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll deal with all of the documents together in the table, isn't it, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I mean, Your Honour, we can do that, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- otherwise it's takes time now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In order to save is little bit more time, as the Prosecution mentioned yesterday, we would like to at least draw the Chamber's attention to some additional documents. Instead of going through 22 more exhibits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- the Prosecution has prepared a list which we can provide to the Chamber after the examination and discussing it with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that material which is already in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is material that is referenced in Mr. Theunens's report. There are some documents which are being opposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objection against ... Apparently you want to draw our attention to certain documents which are directly related to questions put to the witness, is that -- and where you thought that he may have overlooked certain documents which provide useful information on the question, is that, Mr. Weber, what you intend to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And the direct reference would be at page 8467 of the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- in the examination by the Stanisic Defence as to documents relating between Arkan and the SDB and also the MUP of Serbia. Just those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to be practical, of course. At any later stages of the proceedings, of course, you could argue that the information given by the expert witness should be completed by looking at other documents as well, but you now clearly put it in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. And that's all we're doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against proceeding this way?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we should first have a look at the list. But I would like the Trial Chamber to caution the Prosecutor that he should not be testifying and supplementing Mr. Theunens's evidence with his submissions and evidence. I think you observed yesterday that Mr. Weber tried to underpin Mr. Theunens's testimony by referring to certain evidence. And as for the list, I should like to first have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you want to have a look at this list. What I did yesterday was mainly asking Mr. Weber not to intervene during the cross-examination for those purposes, not that he could not draw the attention of the Chamber to certain documents which would shed additional light on certain matters which were subject of the questioning. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I suggest the following, Your Honours: That I would wish to have a break to consider what questions I would like to ask Mr. Theunens in response to the Bozovic and Mijovic re-examination. I don't anticipate that the questions I would like to ask would take longer than 10 minute, but I could certainly do it more efficiently if I could sit down and look at what Mr. Weber has just done, which has completely took me by surprise. And perhaps in the break, if Your Honours are with me on that, we could discuss what Mr. Weber wants to do in relation to this latest suggestion. Because, in relation to the suggestion, if what my learned friend is seeking to do is to say, Well, Mr. Theunens has given a report, he's provided a title and underneath the title offered his support for that proposition, but we the Prosecution now want to say you must look elsewhere in the report in addition to that ... so it's to find additional support for Mr. Theunens' particular proposition; we would oppose that approach. And perhaps we can discuss it outside of court and find out what Mr. Weber wants to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm a bit concerned - it's quarter to 12.00, Mr. Jordash - if you want to have a break now, and I take it that Mr. Stanisic would prefer to be transferred back to the UNDU at 12.00, as scheduled. First of all, I -- I'll discuss with my colleagues whether I agree with you that if Mr. Theunens says, Well, I don't know exactly where or don't remember any documents there and there, whether Mr. Weber would not be in a position to say, but we could assist the Chamber by pointing at certain documents, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I certainly don't oppose that. What I oppose is this: If Mr. Theunens hasn't been able to find a particular reference, of course it's only fair that -- and right, that Your Honours have that pointed out to you. But if Mr. Theunens has come along and written a report which says the Serbian MUP are connected to Arkan, this is how I approach the issue, these are the exhibits which I rely upon; the Defence have come along and then said, well, those exhibits don't support that proposition. And then my learned friends have then gone back to the report and gone to a different part of the report and found other exhibits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We don't have to -- we don't need Mr. Theunens for that at this moment, because you are objecting against a way of proceeding --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- by the Prosecution. We can consider that, whether we would agree with that or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, either Mr. Theunens has done that analysis and listed the analysis under the proposition or he hasn't. Whether there's other support for his proposition --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... well --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... well, Your Honours, just to --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- then that's another issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's -- it's clear you object to the way in which the Prosecution, apart from the questioning of Mr. Theunens, wishes to proceed on these matters. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if -- just to make it short, we're just talking about providing a list. And we rely on what the report says and what the documents say; that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll see. We'll see what will -- what will be presented to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution did have one last matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One last matter, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And it's a matter that I believe we need to address over the break too. With respect to Mr. Theunens's report, we would just like to formally tender it again on the record. It's P1575. We need to upload a corrected version which we will do under 65 ter 5811.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's a technicality. No decision has yet been taken. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would ask that we be allowed to make written submissions on the admissibility of this report. In light of -- we've asked the Prosecution, and Mr. Theunens cannot -- or testifies that he cannot remember what work he did on the Stanisic case. We are waiting for the Prosecution to respond, once they've searched their records, to find out Mr. Theunens' involvement with the Stanisic case outside of the compilation of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has no problems in receiving written submissions on this issue. Mr. Weber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be useful in that situation if the Defence could be expressing what their objection is. So we're just -- it's a very large report that's 426 pages. If they could do that in writing initially and then have us have the opportunity to respond, it would be, I think, more efficient than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I -- yes, of course, it goes without saying Mr. Jordash is still waiting for certain information. Once he has received that information, I take it that he'll make his submissions and then we'll -- written submissions, and there will be an opportunity for you to respond. So I can imagine that in the beginning you would be very -- very short and then that the bulk of your argument would come in response to what Mr. Jordash wants to raise. That seems fair to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, we -- we accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I agree, Your Honour. I can see that Mr. Weber is seated, and I'd like Their Honours to allow me between 10 to 15 minutes because Mr. Weber has raised certain issues that call for re-cross examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, may I take it that you've put all the questions to the witness you intended to put to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. But we -- we would object to a re-cross examination on these documents, especially by the Simatovic Defence on the fact that the Simatovic Defence put questions to the witness related to these individuals and these were documents that were provided to him by the Simatovic Defence in the course of his review for his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's see whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I respond. My time was limited. These are 78 documents. Did I have time to go through all these documents with Mr. Theunens? I did say that I choice those that were a priority to me. And these are all Prosecution documents. Mr. Weber did not raise issues with relation to these documents either in his direct nor did I in my cross do so, but he did so in re-examination, and I don't think it's fair for him to oppose to me having a chance to do so in my re-cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Weber specifically addressed the Mijovic and, to a lesser extent, the Bozovic personnel file, so that certainly is a matter to the extent you have not dealt with that, which, as far as Mr. Mijovic is concerned, is -- by the way, is P1585, formerly known as 2D269 which was admitted into evidence and not under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I thought that at the time it was clear that we -- that the document not be broadcast. I don't think we put on the record at the time that it was under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then P1585, the status now changes; it's admitted under seal. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Only in a brief response that we, the Stanisic Defence, did not deal with Mijovic or Bozovic during our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- that's different. Mijovic was introduced, although not the whole of P1585. Mr. Weber then later found other parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you asked for 10 minutes, and then I'm -- are there any questions you could put to the witness now, or do you need this break? Because we are scheduled to start a videolink this afternoon, and the last thing I could -- well, I would say not dream of, but the real nightmare, certainly for Mr. Theunens, would be to be re-called at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Is it possible just to pause for 10 minutes? It would just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether we have -- first of all, Mr. Stanisic. We specifically scheduled a meeting today to take into account as well the interests of Mr. Stanisic, that there would be sufficient time to return to the UNDU because a normal two half-day session takes more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can try to proceed now as efficiently as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would please try to do so, and then we'll see at the end where we are. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have, please, on e-court 65 ter 4257.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What is going to appear on e-court, Mr. Theunens, is a second request for a check on Bozovic, which is to be found in Bozovic's personnel file. This is the one that Mr. Weber didn't put to you. The one you saw was a request for background -- for a background check dated in 1992, but there is another check which is dated -- sorry, there's another request dated the 16th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to correct the -- one, that we ask that the document not be broadcast; two, that this is just from a different individual's personnel file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a different individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not objecting to the line of questioning though. I understand where Mr. Jordash is going.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, could we have 4257 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps I can try to shortcut this. I think it's fair to say, Mr. Theunens, that there's nothing in Bozovic's file, personnel file, which indicates that the vetting or the background check that was conducted by the Serbian MUP was completed until 1993. And there's nothing in the background -- sorry, there's nothing in the personnel file which indicates that he was employed until after the background check had been completed. Does that in any way --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this a memory test? I mean, I would like to have the copy of the personnel file in order to check. I don't remember -- I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... but you don't --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- there are 192 documents on the CD. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But you don't know what I'm going to ask you yet, so ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but, I mean, I try to understand your question, and in order to understand and to understand your assumptions, I would want to compare them with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: They're not -- I'm just telling you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first -- let's first wait what the question of Mr. Jordash is. Does that in any way, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: On the other hand, we have a document, which we've seen and was put to you by Mr. Weber, where Mr. Bozovic was asserting that he was employed since 1991, and you recall that? We've dealt with it about 15 minutes ago. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He put it in his personal application form. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I have no reason to doubt that it's incorrect. Because if it's incorrect, I would, on the basis of the background checks, I don't think that a candidate who would lie about his pass would still be accepted. I mean, I don't know how it goes into the MUP Serbia, but that's how it works in the UN, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Does the --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And other organisations I've worked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Does the contradiction between what is contained in the personnel file and the assertion by Bozovic not give rise, in your mind, to any doubt as to Mr. Bozovic's assertion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only answer the question, Your Honours, if I had the opportunity to look at the file at its entirety in order to identify any possible inconsistencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I've given you the inconsistency. And if I'm wrong about that, my learned friend Mr. Weber will tell you I'm wrong. There is that inconsistency, and I'm asking you consider it and say whether that in any way makes you reflect on what Mr. Bozovic asserted about his employment since 1991. If you don't want to, that's fine. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a question of wanting; it's a question of -- I try my best to answer your questions, but you put something forward to me, I want to check it. That's how I -- that's -- that's my job as analyst. And in order to be able to check it, I would have to look at the whole file again. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, Mr. Jordash, what you are more or less asking, although with a special eye for Mr. Theunens, is to more or less evaluate the evidence on this matter, which is, of course, fine if an expert does that. Of course, the Chamber has do that as well, if there are certain inconsistencies. Now, what we are therefore seeking at this moment is whether Mr. Theunens has any knowledge at this moment which would allow him to immediately answer and say, No, for this and this reason I consider this inconsistency to be decided in favour of A or B. That's apparently what you're asking him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I understand his answer to be that, I would need to go through all of it, but I do agree that there is some inconsistency which certainly has drawn the attention of the Chamber to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I -- Your Honour, I take the point. Could I just ask then for -- I can shortcut this. Could I just have a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I don't know if you have this knowledge or not, but can you think of any employment benefit which might arise or which might be affected by a claim post facto of being employed for a longer period of time in the Serbian MUP? Let me simplify it. In 1995, can you think of any benefit which might arise or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, let's -- what apparently you want to know is could it have any advantage in lying about your employment --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- pensions, whatever. You could think of that, at least the Chamber could think of that. Do you ever any specific knowledge in this context what kind of benefit someone would have by cheating upon his past in the service?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's the point.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are always people who try to outsmart the system, but I would expect the system to verify this kind of information because apparently there seems to be or there could be an incentive for some less honest people to try to be -- to try to outsmart the system. But, I mean, that's why there is a system, and that's why there are background checks, to check, among other things, the information candidates provide. Because I can imagine if you apply for a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a rather general -- this is, I would say, common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's also common knowledge that if you have accomplices at the right place that you should -- certainly should not deviate from what the fraud is. But then you need others as well. You say it's not that easy, it takes a bit, to defraud -- in order to get those benefits, in order to defraud the system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, my understanding of MUP Serbia - and I haven't analysed it in detail I have to admit I - but I would expect that they would be in a position to verify information of candidates for sensitive positions like memberships or membership of a specialised unit like the special-purpose unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No further questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. Mr. Bakrac, if you can finish in a couple of minutes, because then we don't have to take any specific measures. Otherwise, we'll have to inquire whether Mr. Stanisic and Simatovic wanted to leave and return to the UNDU at this moment. But if it's just a matter of a couple of minutes, then we could give it a try.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll try and focus on the documents that Mr. Weber referred to. Can we have P1585. It's page 32 in B/C/S and page 30 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the document about the incident at the border, the matters raised being the licence plates and ... yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put -- Mr. Theunens will remember, so please immediately put your focused question to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Theunens, it reads here that Vasilije Mijovic introduced himself and said he was a member of the DB. Can you find information therein as to which state security he was a member of?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me which line? I'm trying to find the DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I will try to find it in English. It's line 8 in the second paragraph: [In English] "At the request ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He said that he was a major in the state security.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it now, yes. Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In answer to Mr. Weber's question, you said that this was proof of the fact that he was a major in the Serbian state security. Do you -- can you find it anywhere in this document where it is stated here that he's a major in the Serbian state security?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think we discussed that part with Mr. Weber. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll check that. We'll check that. Next question, please. We'll see what the testimony of Mr. Theunens exactly was. I'll take care of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He states that he is a major in the state security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now, we could speculate why he says that, but, I mean, I don't think that will be of great assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please wait for the next question. Mr. Bakrac, please proceed. I'll check exactly what Mr. Theunens said about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's look at P488 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pages 5 and 6 in B/C/S. And pages 6 and 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Look at page 1. To proceed fast, I'll say that it's the official identification Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 2. So this is an ID paper dated the 21st of March. Can we have page 2, which is pages 6 and 7 in English. Pages 6 and 7 in English. It's pages 6 and 7 in English. Can we have the next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you see that on the 20th of January, 1992, Mr. Vasilije Mijovic was in possession of an official ID of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina? In other words, sometime before the events Mr. Weber discussed with you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, this document states, indeed, the 20th of January, that he has an ID with the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But I think the other document refers to something like November or May 1993, the crossing incident, when we have a totally different situation on the ground. I don't think he would have tried to pass -- I mean, based on my understanding of the situation, I don't think that Mr. Mijovic would have tried to pass the crossing in Mali Zvornik towards Serbia or FRY with showing identity card of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that's just assumption.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But that's based on my understanding of the situation, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I tried to verify in the transcript whether any question was put or whether anything was said about an answer, Mr. Mijovic saying that he was a major in the state security. I did not find any reference to that at all. So, therefore, if you want to revisit it, you will have to indicate exactly what -- where the witness testified about being a major. It, however, draws our attention that apparently in 1993, in this report --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- someone was said to have this rank in the state security, which might need additional attention. Because if there were no ranks, it may cast some doubt. It also -- it's possible that another conclusion should be drawn that there were ranks at the time. We'll carefully consider that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's go back to P1585 now, page 22. This is what Mr. Weber showed you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are talking about the application form, the candidate details. Could you already phrase your first question, Mr. -- and I mean while we are waiting for it to appear on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is information relating to candidates. Mr. Weber showed you what the situation was in the -- in JPAG in -- as of 1991. Do you -- is this a unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, to your mind, or do you allow for the possibility that it may be a unit from a different republic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't analysed the police structures of the different republics in detail, but if it would have been the JATD of another republic, I would have expected that he would have indicated of which republic this JATD was. And again --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's move on because we have to do this fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 28 to see where and when the request was made, -- or the application. Can we have the last page which is page 28 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To proceed quickly, the date is 11 December 1995, in Bijela. Vasilije Mijovic signed it. Do you know where Bijela is? You were in that area, and you may be familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I know a Bijela in Baranja or close to Baranja, there was a crossing, but maybe there is also another Bijela. I can't see the English translation anymore, unfortunately. I touched the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. To your knowledge you know one -- of one Bijela in Baranja. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. In Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have two brief questions. 2D268, please. We want to go back to the issue of Bozovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you already put the question when we are waiting for the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's 268, page 8 in B/C/S and 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What we had on our screens was a proposal to admit Bozovic. Since this is a proposal by Jovica Stanisic, do you know if Bozovic was indeed admitted on this proposal; and if so, when? So we have Milan Radonjic is addressing the Ministry of the Interior and says - look at it - that the anti-terrorist unit was set up on the 4th of August, 1993; whereas in the earlier document by Vasilije Mijovic, we saw JATD from 1991. In my mind, it suggests that this is a different unit; so that's point one. Point two: Do you know if Radojica Bozovic was indeed admitted based on this proposal; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean, there's at least two question, but I don't read this document as if the anti-terrorist unit was established on the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- the Chamber has the establishment of the JATD has been -- let's not -- the simple question is -- but Mr. Bakrac complicates matters a bit, is whether you know whether he was admitted; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I mean, I would have to look at the whole file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then -- yes. Next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two more questions, Your Honour, and I'll finish. Can we move to page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is a request for Podgorica, Tito Grad, from 1992 for the vetting of certain individuals. Do you know when the vetting was conducted and if it resulted in Radojica Bozovic and these other individuals being employed in the state security; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you know, please tell us; if you don't know, please tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know. I mean, we would have to look at the rest of the personnel file in order to establish that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can't answer that question at this moment. Please, next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My understanding was that Mr. Theunens looked at all the personnel files I gave him on a CD over the weekend. Page 5 in B/C/S and 4 in English is the one we should look at next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, we do not expect Mr. Theunens to have learned by heart all of the content of those documents. If there is any other document you have provided to him which gives clearer indication on the matter, then the Chamber certainly will look at it. But we can't require the impossible from this witness at this moment. Please, next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Weber showed you this document. It's a report on a background check or vetting from Radojica Bozovic. And it was in October 1993 that the response came from Podgorica. Do you know if, after this vetting report, Radojica Bozovic was employed in state security; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same answer as to your previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, this was your last question?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there's one thing which we have to finalise, not necessarily in the presence of the accused. I'm a bit concerned that transportation would become difficult if we do not allow the -- the remaining issue is the public character of small parts of the evidence of Mr. Theunens. Perhaps you ask Mr. -- if Mr. Stanisic and Simatovic would prefer to leave at this moment in order to not jeopardise their transfer to the UNDU.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I invite the parties to think about the character of the evidence given in private session on the 26th of October. Mr. Bakrac, when you earlier referred to the 25th, I understood that to be the 26th. Pages 8075 and, after that, 8100 in both cases and following. Is there any intention to make submissions so as to change to the status of - it was only a small portion about -- And perhaps we should turn into private session for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the Prosecution explain the basis for the -- for it to remain in private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, it's about a small portion of the testimony. It is about, I think, the log revolution, but also the involvement in smuggling and -- I think, by a UN official of which the nationality was mentioned. But let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, but even before going there, our position would be that it should remain in private session. But we would like the opportunity to actually discuss the matter with Mr. Theunens after his testimony, because I do not know what the consequences may or may not be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that acceptable that since now we are not talking about the content of the testimony anymore, but we are talking about the reasons why matters should remain confidential or not, that the -- Mr. Weber has an opportunity to briefly discuss it with Mr. Theunens, that we later then hear submissions, most likely oral submissions, on the matter, and that then we'll finally decide? It seems not to be a vital and core issue in the whole of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, you agree as well? You agree as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. Thank you. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm a bit hesitant to accept that someone who remains silent has agreed to what was said. Mr. Theunens, this concludes your testimony. You'll have an opportunity to speak about the matter we just raised with Mr. Weber. We'll take seriously into consideration whatever reasons there are to leave matters as they are at this moment or to change the status of that part of your testimony. We've kept you busy for quite a while, it must -- I take it that, having worked for quite a while in this institution, you must have felt at home; but, nevertheless, it might have been a bit long. And perhaps you have a new home these days. Therefore, I would like to thank you very much not only for coming but also for staying for such a long time with us. And I wish you a safe return home to your -- to the place what is your home now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could Mr. Theunens be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any matters to be urgently raised before we adjourn? Because we'll -- we'd like to see you back in two hours and four minutes from now. Any matters? Could I ask the parties to see to it to find a practical arrangement for all the documents which we have left undecided at this moment, to see whether you can agree. If not, then, of course, the Chamber will see whether the suggestions it made will become rulings. We adjourn and we resume at 2.30 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.27 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. We start this afternoon in open session. I failed to -- when adjourning, I failed to move into open session again. I hereby inform the public that where we should have returned into open session was at the moment where I thanked Mr. Theunens for coming and for answering the questions and he then was excused. Having said this, we turn into closed session because we'll hear the evidence of the next witness in closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I would like to invite the parties to prepare the tables for the document used with the previous witness. If there are any further submissions to be made in relation to the admissibility of the last witness, the Chamber would like to receive them on shortest notice, that is, not later than by next week, Wednesday. We adjourn until Tuesday the 9th of November, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of November, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
